title: Adaptive iterator orchestration, halt policy, and output normalization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Multi-tool chains that mix streaming responses, function/tool calling, and structured-output contracts are causing two classes of failures in production: (1) runaway recursion/loops when tools re-invoke the core agent with overlapping prompts or when result injection re-triggers tool selection; (2) schema drift where streaming partials and legacy compatibility layers produce outputs that fail downstream strict validators. Goal: Design and implement an adaptive iterator / orchestration layer that enforces halt policies (both heuristic and deterministic), normalizes tool outputs into a canonical envelope for downstream validators, and provides a compatibility shim to accept legacy tool-call shapes while preserving streaming UX and idempotency guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Iterator enforces a per-request and per-tool token/step budget with deterministic halting when limits are exceeded
Tool results are wrapped in a canonical envelope (metadata, provenance, idempotency token, schema-version) before injection into the prompt or call stack
Streaming partials are buffered and normalized so structured output validators only run on completed envelopes or safe incremental checkpoints
Recursion detector flags loops above configured thresholds and triggers a safe fallback: cancel further tool selection and allow a graceful synthesized summary response
Compatibility shim accepts legacy function-call payloads (legacy name/args) and maps to current structured schema with telemetry showing conversion rates
E2E test harness reproduces previously observed runaway loop case and demonstrates deterministic halt and safe fallback
tech_notes: Halt policy: combine static limits (max_tool_steps, max_token_budget) with dynamic heuristics (repeated tool-id patterns, decreasing information delta) to estimate diminishing returns and trigger halting earlier for long chains

Recursion detection: maintain a lightweight call-signature stack for each request (tool name + normalized args hash + last-output-hash). If a signature repeats > threshold within sliding window, mark as potential loop. Use exponential backoff penalty to prevent immediate repeated retries.

Canonical envelope: {"schema_version":"1.0", "tool":..., "provenance":..., "idempotency_token":..., "payload":...} — note: store as flat JSON string for streaming to avoid nested parse issues in older SDKs

Streaming normalization: buffer streaming tokens until boundary markers (explicit <END_OUTPUT> or schema field completion). For very long streaming outputs, allow incremental checkpoints annotated with partial=true and validator-friendly placeholders

Compatibility layer: implement mapping rules (legacy_field_name -> canonical_field_name) and an optional strict_mode flag. When not strict, fallback to best-effort mapping and attach conversion_warnings to envelope metadata

KV cache interactions: canonical envelopes must include cache keys for prefix/KV reuse. Ensure that result injection does not create cache thrash by deduplicating identical idempotency tokens within window
Observability: emit events: iterator.step_start, iterator.step_halt, tool.injected_envelope, loop_detected, compatibility_mapped with correlation ids. Include token and time_cost metrics
decisions: Deterministic halting has priority over speculative continuation to guarantee SLOs
Canonical envelope will be a single-line JSON string to maximize compatibility with older consoles and streaming parsers
Compatibility shim will be opt-out per-customer to avoid unexpected behavior for strict enterprise integrations
When loop detected, prefer synthesized summary fallback over silent cancellation to maintain UX
test_plan: Unit tests for signature stack creation, hashing, and repeat-detection with synthetic chains
Integration test: reproduce production loop sequence and assert iterator halts and returns synthesized summary; assert no tool executed after halting
Streaming test: simulate interleaved tool streaming + function-calls and verify validators only run on completed canonical envelopes
Compatibility tests: run mapped legacy payloads through shim and assert payload normalization and attached conversion_warnings
Load test: verify per-request halting scales under 500 RPS with no regression in median latency for short chains
